jia: heads up — after the int8 bring-up (v2-quant) on staging I'm seeing a consistent BLEU drop on the multilingual regression suite :thinking:

jia: quick numbers: zh->en baseline(v1) BLEU=28.3, v2-int8 BLEU=24.1. ar->en 31.2 -> 27.5. ja->en 25.6 -> 22.0. overall delta ~ -3.8 BLEU points

sara: ugh. did anything else land besides quant kernels? tokenization/normalization changes?

jia: the bring-up PR touched a small tokenizer flag: normalize_unicode=True was turned on for the new runtime path (to simplify kernel char handling). suspected it might affect CJK/ZWJ/width handling

eva: that flag sounds risky. can you diff tokenizer outputs between v1 and v2 for failing examples?

jia: already ran a quick diff on the eval set. examples show halfwidth/fullwidth punctuation flips and some extra ZWJ being removed. sample diffs:

```
# example zh input: 这是「测试」 — v1 token ids: [345, 987, 44, 999] 
# v2 tokens: [345, 987, 44, 1001]  # different mapping for the corner quotes
# ja case: ASCII punctuation normalized to fullwidth in v1 but to ascii in v2 -> token boundary shifts
```

sara: that would shift IDs and KV cache offsets — plausible cause of quality regressions even if logits mostly preserved

mike: can you paste the exact tokenizer config used for v1 vs v2? I want to check normalization + pretokenize steps

jia: v1 config: `normalize_unicode=False, pretokenize_jpn_kan=False, use_zwj_preserve=True`

jia: v2 config (runtime path): `normalize_unicode=True, pretokenize_jpn_kan=False, use_zwj_preserve=False`

sara: there — `use_zwj_preserve` flipped off and unicode normalization on. that combo will collapse some grapheme sequences and change tokenization in mixed-script sentences

eva: can we reproduce exact BLEU delta on a tiny subset reliably? if yes, we can bisect which change caused it (norm vs zwj flag)

jia: minimal repro I used: 200-sent subset from multilang-xl. repro command:

```bash
./eval_suite --model v1 --dataset small-multilang > v1.out
./eval_suite --model v2 --dataset small-multilang > v2.out
python3 -c "from sacrebleu import corpus_bleu; print(corpus_bleu(open('v2.out').read().splitlines(), [open('v1.ref').read().splitlines()]))"
```

mike: i'll spin a quick job that toggles normalization and zwj flags independently on the runtime image and run the 200-sent check. ping me if you want raw token diffs

ci-bot: scheduled regression job #ml-1985550000 started: 200-sent quick-check (v1 vs v2) — ETA ~12m

sara: hypothesis: unicode NFC/NFD normalization + zwj removal changes grapheme boundaries -> token id shift -> LM sees different prefix -> larger downstream generation differences for CJK & Arabic punctuation-heavy sentences

eva: in the short term can we rollback the tokenizer change on staging while we triage? customers might hit this in dedicated/private as well

mike: can revert a flag flip without full rollback — patching runtime config now and kicking new staging workers

mike: done — patched `normalize_unicode=False` and `use_zwj_preserve=True` on staging pool, redeploying :rocket:

ci-bot: regression job #ml-1985550000 finished. quick summary:
- v2 (original flags) vs v1: zh->en BLEU delta -4.2
- v2 (norm=False, zwj_preserve=True) vs v1: zh->en BLEU delta -0.3
- conclusion: tokenizer flags explain most of the regression

jia: excellent — confirms the tokenization hypothesis. thanks mike + ci-bot

sara: next steps: 1) revert the change in mainline PR, 2) add explicit tokenization regression tests for mixed-width punctuation + zwj cases, 3) add a gating check for tokenizer config drift in compile/runtime code paths

eva: also add a note to the private deployment docs: changing unicode normalization can be a breaking change for customers with locale-sensitive corpora

jia: i'll open a PR to revert + add tests. linking the failing examples and the quick-check harness in the PR description

sara: cc @eng-runtime — we should ensure compile-time optimizations don't silently change normalization semantics

mike: will follow up with a small runtime patch that keeps kernel optimizations but preserves tokenization semantics by default

jia: thanks everyone. leaving open until PR merges but staging is back to baseline for now :thumbsup:
